standard_prerequisites.name: Log geometry, toroidal resolution and weak Neron models
standard_prerequisites.statement: Author uses Kato log-smooth/log-regular geometry, toroidal fan modifications and the regular-proper-model smooth locus weak-Neron result (BLR). The paper own base-change/multiplicity/weight/tame-degree proofs are explicitly supplied as core; external standard theorems remain named inputs, not recursively reproved.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lang-Weil and Stone-Weierstrass
standard_prerequisites.statement: Finite-field stratum point counts use the author cited Lang-Weil estimates; model-function density uses Stone-Weierstrass after the included separation proof. The nonroutine uniform weighted-polytope convergence is the fully included author Lemma6.5.1.

core_obligations: Retain both original model hypotheses and normalized measures; do not replace tame snc case by all-extensions claim
Retain the full weighted lattice concentration proof and geometric upper/lower tube-to-stratum estimates
Retain tame-degree/stable-measure and weight/base-change core; count one author ramified-convergence parent rather than every supporting lemma
proof_roadmap: Reduce weak convergence to vertical model functions and adapt them via toroidal modification.
Pass to normalized base change with controlled multiplicities/geometrically connected strata, retaining the stable measure scaling.
Bound local-field integrals by finite-field stratum counts and combine Lang-Weil with the uniform polytope concentration lemma.
Apply the author reduced log-smooth base-change argument for all finite extensions.
difficulty_reason: H3: the author couples logarithmic/toroidal model geometry, weight-function and skeleton behavior under ramified base change, tame-degree-weighted Lebesgue measures, weak-Neron tube integral estimates, Lang-Weil stratum asymptotics and a uniform two-parameter lattice concentration argument. The proof must control the ramification scaling and the distinct tame/all-extension hypotheses while reducing weak convergence to adapted model functions. All local nonroutine core is retained under one parent, beyond a routine consequence or direct Riemann sum.
